html:
The human rights treaty of Africa, adopted by the Organisation of African Unity in Nairobi in June 1981 and in force from 1986. It is also called the Banjul Charter, after Banjul in the Gambia, where it was drafted.

It protects the familiar rights to life, fair trial, free speech and religion found in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. But it adds two things that set it apart:

  • Rights of peoples, not just individuals: to exist, to choose their own government, to develop, to control their wealth and resources, and to a satisfactory environment.
  • Duties of individuals toward their family, community and state.

The charter set up the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, based in Banjul. Later an African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights was added, sitting in Arusha, and the Maputo Protocol of 2003 added the rights of women. Almost every member of the African Union has ratified it, though many governments ignore the rulings made under it.
sum: The human rights treaty of Africa, adopted by the Organisation of African Unity in Nairobi in June 1981 and in force from 1986. It is also called the Banjul Charter, after Banjul in the Gambia, where it was drafted.
